verdict_reason: REVERSING MY OWN PRIOR RED. Both R14 fixes verified by direct re-measurement. (1) Vocabulary preservation is now exactly true: replaying the OLD code path (encode(add_special_tokens=False) -> shuffle -> decode -> re-tokenize at max_length=128) on the first 50 WikiText-103 validation passages, the multiset the model was fed differed from the shuffled multiset in 41/50 texts for gpt2, 41/50 for pythia-70m, 41/50 for pythia-160m and 41/50 for distilgpt2; under the CURRENT in-place-ids path the multiset fed to the model is an exact permutation of the ID sample's in 50/50 texts for all four tokenizers (0/50 mismatches, 0/50 identity permutations). (2) The scoring kernel is bit-exact against the authors' released code: scipy.spatial.distance.mahalanobis(x, mu, LedoitWolf.precision_) equals Lee et al.'s sqrt(-2*term_gau) to 0.000e+00 absolute and relative, and sklearn's precision_ equals inv(covariance_) to 8.4e-16 with location_ == np.mean(X_train,0). (3) The held-out/paired split does what the code says: every model I ran reports n_id_fit=25, n_id_score=25, n_ood_score=25, i.e. the covariance is fitted on texts that are neither scored as ID nor shuffled into the OOD set. Judged against the definition the task DECLARES in task_metadata.py -- a single-centroid C=1 Ledoit-Wolf refined-adaptation of Lee et al., not Eq. 2 -- the code computes exactly that quantity, so verdict is GREEN and the estimator objections below are recorded as validity/comparability findings, not implementation infidelity.
comparable_reason: Three independent mechanisms, all re-measured this round. (a) The raw statistic is mechanically width-scaled: under a pure iid N(0,I_d) null at the shipped protocol (n_fit=25, n_score=25, no model in the loop) mean_mahalanobis rises 8.364 -> 11.910 -> 16.936 -> 24.143 -> 29.686 -> 34.420 for d = 64/128/256/512/768/1024, tracking sqrt(d) to within 4.5-7.6% (Spearman +1.000). (b) Models are not scored by the SAME FUNCTION: realised Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage on the identical shipped protocol spans 0.0643 (gpt2-medium) to 0.6056 (pythia-70m) across 9 freshly run models, a 9.4x spread, and it is itself width-linked (rho = -0.411). Shrinking toward an isotropic target destroys the affine invariance that makes a Mahalanobis distance meaningful: under a diagonal rescale x -> Ax (logspace(0,3), d=64, n_fit=25) the LedoitWolf distances move by up to 41.9% of their mean and the sample ORDERING changes (Spearman 0.270 pre- vs post-rescale), whereas EmpiricalCovariance at n=400 > d=64 is invariant to 9.4e-12. (c) The consequence is visible as a 90x discontinuity between two models of IDENTICAL width: at d=1024, gpt2-medium gives mean_mahalanobis_id 4.88 / mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id 0.0237 / shrinkage 0.0643 / auroc 0.9968 while pythia-410m gives 45.08 / 2.1219 / 0.5238 / 0.7616. Across the 9 models mean_mahalanobis_id spans 4.88-45.08 (9.2x). The purely correlational picture is now much WEAKER than the stale 61-model archive implied: over 9 fresh models rho(auroc, d_model) = +0.490 (p = 0.18), rho(auroc, n_layers) = +0.199, rho(auroc, log n_params) = +0.383, against +0.742 / +0.680 / +0.788 measured last round on the pre-fix archive. RED is driven by (a)-(c), not by the correlations.
normalized_ok_detail: MEASURED on both an analytic null and 9 real models, and it does the job it was designed for while leaving the bigger problem untouched. Width scaling: under the iid Gaussian null at n_fit=25, raw mean_mahalanobis grows 4.11x over d = 64 -> 1024 while dist^2/d moves only 1.1018 -> 1.1575 (+5.1%), i.e. ~98.8% of the mechanical width scaling is removed; on the 9 real models rho(mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id, d_model) = -0.105 and rho(ood_separation_gap_per_dim, d_model) = -0.061, against +0.315 for mean_mahalanobis_id and +0.472 for ood_separation_ratio. So as a de-scaler it works and it is a strict improvement on ood_separation_ratio. Two things keep it off GREEN. First, the code comment at mahalanobis.py:398-401 asserts dist^2/d 'has expectation 1 regardless of d'; at the shipped n_fit=25 the iid-null value is 1.1018 at d=64 rising monotonically to 1.1575 at d=1024, a 10-16% estimation bias, and on real models the value ranges 0.0237-2.3371. Second, and decisively, the per-dim form does nothing about the estimator heterogeneity: mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id spans 98.6x across the 9 models and 90x between two models of the SAME width (gpt2-medium 0.0237 vs pythia-410m 2.1219 at d=1024), so its spread is covariance-estimation regime, not geometry. Note also that the FIX NOTE'S OWN NUMBERS DO NOT REPRODUCE at the shipped defaults (fp32, WikiText-103 validation, max_length=128): I measure gpt2 mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id = 1.4552 (claimed 1.085), gpt2 shrinkage 0.0678 (claimed 0.061) and pythia-70m shrinkage 0.6056 (claimed 0.268 -- 0.606 is what the previous round measured). Only _meta_d_over_n_fit = 30.72 on gpt2 matches the claimed 30.7.
github_reason: Re-fetched lib_generation.py (409 lines) from the authors' repo this round. sample_estimator (lines 45-124) computes PER-CLASS means and fits sklearn.covariance.EmpiricalCovariance(assume_centered=False) on the POOLED within-class residuals concatenated over classes; get_Mahalanobis_score (lines 126-198) computes term_gau = -0.5 * zero_f @ precision @ zero_f.T for every class, takes gaussian_score.max(1), then applies FGSM-style input preprocessing at magnitude and a multi-layer logistic-regression ensemble. Head-to-head on the kernel at C=1 with matched precision: BLME == sqrt(-2*term_gau) to 0.000e+00 (exact, better than the 3.11e-15 recorded last round). I could NOT run the released pipeline end to end (legacy CUDA DenseNet/ResNet checkpoints and PyTorch-0.4-era Variable API), hence PARTIAL. BLME departs from the reference in estimator (single global centroid + LedoitWolf, no max over classes) and protocol (no input preprocessing, no layer ensemble, no labels); that departure is declared in task_metadata.py as a 'refined-adaptation ... single-centroid C=1 adaptation with Ledoit-Wolf', though NOT in the module or class docstring, which still list Lee et al. 2018 under a bare 'References'.
paper_reason: Lee et al. 2018 publish TNR/AUROC/detection-accuracy for CIFAR-10/100 and SVHN in-distribution against TinyImageNet/LSUN/SVHN OOD and FGSM/BIM/DeepFool/CW adversarial detection, on trained DenseNet and ResNet classifiers WITH labels, using per-class means and input preprocessing. There is no published number for a label-free single-centroid Mahalanobis score on mean-pooled language-model hidden states with a token-shuffled OOD set, so the paper offers no target this task's output could reproduce.
confounds_reason: CONFIRMED for the distance fields, and analytically rather than correlationally: with NO model in the loop, an iid N(0,I_d) null at the shipped n_fit=25 gives mean_mahalanobis 8.364 (d=64) -> 34.420 (d=1024), Spearman +1.000 with d and within 7.6% of sqrt(d) throughout, so mean_mahalanobis_id / _ood carry a width term that has nothing to do with the model. The realised shrinkage is also width-linked (rho(shrinkage, d_model) = -0.411 over 9 models). The headline auroc, however, is now only weakly size-associated: over 9 freshly re-run models (distilgpt2, pythia-70m, gpt2, pythia-160m, opt-125m, gpt2-medium, pythia-410m, Qwen2.5-0.5B, SmolLM2-135M) rho(auroc, d_model) = +0.490 (p = 0.18), rho(auroc, n_layers) = +0.199, rho(auroc, log n_params) = +0.383. That is a REAL WEAKENING relative to the +0.742 / +0.680 / +0.788 I measured last round on the 61-model archive, and it is attributable to the fix: the archive was produced by the unpaired, decode-round-tripped design. I am partially refuting my own prior confound finding here.
defects: The estimator is not Lee et al.'s and inverts on multimodal ID clouds. Re-measured over 20 seeds on a bimodal ID cloud in R^8 (modes at +/-10 e1) with OOD at the GLOBAL mean: BLME's single-centroid score gives mean AUROC 0.0212 (range 0.0065-0.0463) while Lee et al.'s per-class means + pooled within-class EmpiricalCovariance + max-over-classes gives 1.0000 on every seed. Sentence representations are multimodal by topic, so this is not a corner case. This is a DECLARED design adaptation (task_metadata: 'single-centroid C=1'), which is why it is not scored as an implementation defect -- but it is a code-level choice with no config switch, so any fix is a CODE change, not a CONFIG one.

Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage breaks affine invariance and makes the scoring function model-dependent. Under a diagonal rescale the LedoitWolf distances change by up to 41.9% of their mean and reorder (Spearman 0.270), vs 9.4e-12 invariance for EmpiricalCovariance at n>d; realised shrinkage spans 0.0678 (gpt2) to 0.6056 (pythia-70m) on the identical shipped protocol. Also a CODE-level declared choice, not a CONFIG value: there is no config key that selects the estimator.

The new dimension-calibration comment overclaims. mahalanobis.py:398-401 says dist^2/d 'has expectation 1 regardless of d'; at the shipped n_fit=25 the iid-null value is 1.1018 (d=64) rising monotonically to 1.1575 (d=1024). The statistic is a good relative de-scaler (removes ~98.8% of the sqrt(d) growth) but it is not calibrated to 1.

The numbers in the R14 fix note do not reproduce at the shipped defaults (fp32, WikiText-103 validation, max_length=128): gpt2 mahalanobis_sq_per_dim_id = 1.4552 not 1.085; gpt2 shrinkage = 0.0678 not 0.061; pythia-70m shrinkage = 0.6056 not 0.268. The pre-fix mismatch count for pythia-70m is 41/50 under a faithful replay of the old code (39/50 if both sides are truncated first, 40/50 for the pure round trip with no truncation) -- not 43/50. Only _meta_d_over_n_fit = 30.72 matches.

Estimator instability at the shipped n_fit=25: gpt2-medium returns mean_mahalanobis_id = 4.88 in d=1024 where every other model returns 28.7-45.1, with shrinkage 0.0643 and auroc 0.9968. A 9.2x range in the ID distance across 9 models, and a 90x gap between two d=1024 models, means the reported distances are not on a common scale. CONFIG in the sense that raising n_id_fit above d would remove it; CODE in the sense that the LedoitWolf choice is hard-wired.

EVERY ARCHIVED geometry_mahalanobis VALUE IS STALE and must be re-collected. The archive carries n_ood_score = 50 (unpaired second-half OOD) against the current 25, and no _meta_/per-dim fields at all. Re-running the current code moves pythia-70m AUROC 0.764 -> 0.6448 (-0.119) and its ood_separation_gap 3.868 -> 2.337 (-40%); gpt2 0.944 -> 0.9296; pythia-160m gap 6.082 -> 9.095 (+50%).

defaults.yaml sets num_samples: 50, which after the half-split leaves the covariance fitted on n=25 in d=512-8192 (_meta_d_over_n_fit = 20.5 on pythia-70m, 30.7 on gpt2/distilgpt2/pythia-160m/opt-125m), i.e. a rank-24 empirical covariance. This is a CONFIG defect; the code now surfaces it honestly via _meta_d_over_n_fit and _meta_n_cov_fit.

The C=1 adaptation is disclosed in task_metadata.py but NOT in mahalanobis.py's module or class docstring, which still list 'Lee et al., NeurIPS 2018' under a bare 'References' heading with no note that the estimator is single-centroid and shrunk.

No regression test pins the vocabulary-preservation property that this round just fixed; tests/tasks/test_mahalanobis_task.py (5 tests, all passing) covers only the held-out split and the leverage bias.
